clue.text: Its instruments confound the management

parts.note: in the old oath 'dash it!' to dash is to confound or curse
the board of directors is the management of a company

explanation.surface: Somebody curses the bosses of a firm and the tools they work with.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is oblique: the thing is identified by what it carries, the dials and gauges in front of a driver. 'Confound' is the mild curse, as in 'dash it all'.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's front panel is where the speedometer and other gauges sit, so it is known by the dials it holds.

clue.text: Spoke grandly of Continental medical treatment

parts.note: de is French for of, the Continental version of the word

indicators.note: a treatment works the letters over, giving them a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Somebody holds forth about European health care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medical treatment' reads as one phrase, but 'treatment' is the anagram sign, turning MEDICAL into CLAIMED.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate in a rhetorical, theatrical way is to speak grandly.

clue.text: Irishman died in the midst of this battle

indicators.note: one piece placed in the midst of another goes inside it

parts.note: Sean is a typically Irish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irish soldier was killed in the thick of a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The battle is the French defeat by Prussia in 1870, at a town on the Meuse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Franco-Prussian War's decisive 1870 battle took its name from this French town.

clue.text: Force makes a speculator nod

parts.note: a bull is a stock-market speculator who buys expecting prices to rise
to nod is to doze, nodding off

explanation.surface: A tired investor is pushed into falling asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: On the stock market a bull speculates on a rise. 'nod' means to drowse, not a gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: To push through by sheer power, as a heavy earthmover does.

clue.text: Getting together to compose a sacred work in a simple key

parts.note: a mass is a sacred choral composition
G major has only one sharp, an easy key

explanation.surface: A composer gathers ideas for a church setting in a plain key.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests writing a Mass in G; the pieces are exactly that phrase, A MASS IN G, read as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Accumulating or collecting, as in gathering a fortune.

clue.text: Order upset youngster with tangled mass in hair

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, read from the bottom up

parts.note: a kid is a youngster
a tat is a tangle or knot in hair

explanation.surface: A distressed child has a knot of matted hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree imposed by an authority is a command.

clue.text: Honour accepted by a female poet

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a female
the OM, Order of Merit, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A woman writer is given an award from the state.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, an honour given by the British monarch. The surface suggests a female poet; the poet is in fact the Greek epic author.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek author of the Iliad and Odyssey is the archetypal epic versifier.

clue.text: Officer maintained accommodation for gunners

indicators.note: a word giving accommodation to another houses it, so one goes inside

parts.note: held means maintained, as in held a view
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: An officer kept up quarters for the artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, the Royal Artillery, are the British Army's gunners. The officer is one of arms, who rules on coats of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: An official of arms, who once carried royal messages, is a state functionary.

clue.text: Unusually remote object, originally extraterrestrial

indicators.note: letters arranged unusually are in an odd order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: it is the pronoun for an object

indicators.note: originally points to the opening of the next word

explanation.surface: A distant thing that began its journey in outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unusually' rearranges REMOTE with IT (object) to make METEORIT; 'originally' gives the E from 'extraterrestrial'. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rock that fell to earth from space is a far-flung body from beyond our world.

clue.text: Storm crossing northern mountains

indicators.note: one word crossing another spans it, so the second sits inside the first

parts.note: to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: Bad weather sweeps across the northern peaks.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain of mountains is a mountain range.

clue.text: Subscription from a Paris underwriter?

parts.note: read literally, a sub-script is a mark written under a letter, and a Parisian writer puts this hook beneath a c

explanation.surface: An insurer in France pays a membership fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subscription' and 'underwriter' both point to money and insurance; split them as sub-script and under-writer and they describe a mark a French writer places below a letter, as in garçon.
explanation.definitionFit: This hook-shaped diacritic sits beneath a c in French spelling to show it is said like an s.

clue.text: Green parrot can run inside compound-it helps its claws

indicators.note: the run goes inside the parrot, one piece placed within the other

parts.note: the kea is an olive-green parrot of New Zealand
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A green bird in a cage is fed a substance that strengthens its talons.
explanation.walkthrough: The kea is a large olive-green New Zealand parrot. The definition runs on from 'compound': the protein is what the bird's own claws are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: This fibrous protein forms hair, horn, nails and the talons of birds.

clue.text: A Welsh fellow is so bristly

parts.note: Ned is a man's name, used for any fellow

explanation.surface: A man from Wales has a stubbly chin.
explanation.definitionFit: An awn is a stiff bristle on an ear of grain, so a plant having them is bristly.

clue.text: Like a firearm the sergeant-major, a man about fifty, carried

parts.note: SM is the usual abbreviation for sergeant-major

indicators.note: one piece is placed about, around, another, so it goes inside

parts.note: Al is a man's name
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
bore is the past tense of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: A soldier's weapon, borne by the sergeant-major and a man of about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts L (fifty) inside AL (a man), giving ALL either way round. 'Like a firearm' is a hedge: the word describes a gun of narrow calibre.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle of narrow calibre, such as a .22, is described by this term for its slim barrel.

clue.text: Publication for the powder-room

definitions.meaning: a periodical such as a glossy weekly
a store for gunpowder and ammunition, as on a warship or in a fort

explanation.surface: A periodical left lying in the ladies' cloakroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powder-room' suggests a ladies' lavatory, where such reading might lie about; here it is a room for gunpowder.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a periodical and an ammunition store on a ship or in a fort go by this name.

clue.text: Set up house in Georgia, starting not to gad about

indicators.note: the house goes in Georgia, one piece inside the other

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: a villa is a house

indicators.note: starting takes the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Someone settles down in the American South, resolving to stop roaming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reverses VILLA to ALLIV, put in GA; 'starting' takes the first letters of 'not to', NT.
explanation.definitionFit: To wander about seeking pleasure is to roam or run around.

clue.text: Object to wits

definitions.meaning: to object is to take exception, as in 'do you object if I smoke'
one's wits are one's intelligence or mental faculties

explanation.definitionFit: To dislike or take exception is one sense; the intellect or reason is the other.

clue.text: Apollyon's vessel

definitions.meaning: in Revelation, Apollyon is the angel of the bottomless pit, his name meaning the one who ruins
a fast warship of the navy

explanation.surface: The devil's own ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Apollyon, in the Book of Revelation, is the angel whose name means one who lays waste.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek name Apollyon means one who ruins, and a fast naval warship shares the word.

clue.text: Bad way to rule, almost leading to banishment

indicators.note: bad means faulty, so the letters are set out wrongly, rearranged
almost means not quite, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Tyranny is a poor way to govern, nearly ending in exile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims RULE to RUL; 'Bad' rearranges WAY, TO and RUL together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being declared outside the law's protection was a form of exile.

clue.text: Wandering musician — the last in Scott's lay?

definitions.meaning: Walter Scott's poem The Lay of the Last ___ is named after its old harper

explanation.surface: A travelling singer, the final figure of a Scott poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Walter Scott's 1805 narrative poem is The Lay of the Last ___: its title names the last of these singers.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval travelling entertainer, and the subject of Scott's 1805 narrative poem.

clue.text: Robot abandoned a thousand in the valley

indicators.note: something abandoned is dropped, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: a Dalek is the robot-like villain of Doctor Who
K stands for a thousand, as in kilo

explanation.surface: A mechanical man is left behind with a grand in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daleks are the metal-cased villains of the British TV series Doctor Who. 'abandoned' takes K away from DALEK.
explanation.definitionFit: This word, common in northern English place names, means a broad river valley.

clue.text: Functions held by transport company

indicators.note: something held by another sits within it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport
sine is a trigonometric function, plural sines

explanation.surface: Social events are put on by a haulage firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Functions' looks like parties, but it means the trigonometric sines, put inside BUS between U and S.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm or commercial concern is a synonym for a trading company.

clue.text: Change in male domestic

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man's housework routine is altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant doing humble household work is a domestic.

clue.text: Half of them support an Italian family, showing great respect

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: the Este were a noble family ruling Ferrara

indicators.note: half of a four-letter word drops two letters, here its first pair

explanation.surface: Half the people back a noble Italian dynasty, showing deep regard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Este were the Renaissance rulers of Ferrara. EM, the second half of THEM, goes below ESTE.
explanation.definitionFit: High regard or admiration is a synonym for great respect.

clue.text: Vain rules made all-embracing

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new arrangement, reworked to form another word

explanation.surface: Pointless regulations were imposed on everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Something covering every case without exception is comprehensive or general.

clue.text: States, say, overturned customary practice

parts.note: the USA, the United States

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturned means turned upside down, read from the bottom up

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: America, for example, overturned a long-standing tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: Established habit or custom is the way something is usually done.

clue.text: Direct one's course in Hereford, possibly

definitions.meaning: to guide the way one is heading
the Hereford is a breed of beef cattle, and a young castrated bull of it is one example

explanation.surface: Someone plots a route through the English town of Hereford.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is an English cathedral city, but here it is the red-and-white beef breed named after it; 'possibly' marks the example.
explanation.definitionFit: To guide a vehicle is one sense; a bullock raised for beef is the other.

clue.text: Furnish quarters to hold party

indicators.note: something made to hold another contains it, so one goes inside

parts.note: east, north and west are compass quarters
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Someone provides rooms to host a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings; it is three compass points, E, N and W, holding DO.
explanation.definitionFit: To provide with an income or quality, as a donor does a college.

clue.text: Greediness of a state supplied with grain

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia
rice is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: A nation is accused of hoarding its cereal harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe after the first word is a speck on the page. VA is Virginia, one of the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive desire for wealth is greed, one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Mundane and verbose — twice interrupted by students

indicators.note: twice means the students break in a second time, at another point in the word
a word interrupted by others has them breaking into it, so pieces go inside

parts.note: wordy means using too many words
L is a learner, the student driver's plate
L is a learner, the student driver's plate

explanation.surface: Someone dull and long-winded keeps being cut off by pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' gives two Ls (learners), and 'interrupted by' breaks WORDY in two places: one L after WOR, the other after D.
explanation.definitionFit: Concerned with material, earthly affairs rather than spiritual ones.

clue.text: Once retired, many receive praise

parts.note: ex- means former, what one once was

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going back, so the word for many is read backwards

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Former employees, now pensioned off, are given a tribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' is the reversal sign on LOT, giving TOL; 'receive' only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To laud or speak highly of someone is a synonym for acclaiming them.

clue.text: A bloomer associated with English Puritans?

definitions.meaning: hawthorn blossom, a plant flowering in late spring
the ship that carried the Pilgrim Fathers to New England in 1620

explanation.surface: A flower tied in some way to strict English Protestants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder; it is a flowering plant, the hawthorn. The Pilgrim Fathers were Puritans who sailed in 1620.
explanation.definitionFit: Hawthorn blossom bears this name, as did the Pilgrim Fathers' ship of 1620.
